reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) concerns an fcc-based Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy, not the BCC TiVNbTa refractory HEA, and demonstrates precipitation at 580°C (853 K), far below the proposed 1273 K service temperature. It provides no support for the key premises regarding precipitation, stability, or strengthening in the TiVNbTa system at 1273 K.
premises: TiVNbTa can be precipitation-hardened by heat treatment to form nanoscale coherent precipitates
Such precipitates will remain stable and coherent at 1273 K
These precipitates will effectively impede dislocation motion and climb at 1273 K
The resulting strength increase will be substantial (from ~330 MPa to ≥500 MPa)
